claims.text: GDACS's event report for 'Flood in Sri Lanka' (event id 1104075, source GLOFAS, overall Green alert, reporting window 02 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC to 04 Aug 2026 01:00 UTC) records via its Sendai indicator feed: 8 fatalities in Sri Lanka and 4 fatalities specifically in Hatton (12 total); 3,316 people evacuated plus 3,566 more evacuated (6,882 total); 15,412 people / 1,512 households affected; 537 and 129 buildings damaged (666 total); and 21 people rescued in Gampola.

DMC Situation Report — Sri Lanka, 17 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL — 4,214 Families / 16,555 People Affected; Deaths 9; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 718 Partially (720 total); Safe Locations: 2 locations, 16 families, 47 persons — down sharply from 9 locations / 52 families / 188 persons on 14 August, indicating displaced people returning home. Nuwara Eliya district remains worst-hit (2,021 families / 7,736 people affected, 6 deaths), followed by Kandy district (1,183 families / 4,925 people affected, 2 deaths).

DMC Situation Report -- Sri Lanka, 19 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL -- 4,222 Families / 16,583 People Affected; Deaths 9; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 723 Partially (725 total); Safe Locations: 2 locations, 16 families, 47 persons -- unchanged from the 17 August 2026 sheltered-population figure, with affected families/houses-damaged ticking up only slightly (4,214->4,222 families; 720->725 houses damaged). Nuwara Eliya district remains worst-hit (2,021 families / 7,736 people affected, 6 deaths), followed by Kandy district (1,183 families / 4,925 people affected, 2 deaths). GDACS's event report (FL 1104075, episode 1) remains unchanged and static since 6 August.

DMC Situation Report -- Sri Lanka, 23 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL -- 4,232 Families / 16,614 People Affected; Deaths 9; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 733 Partially (735 total); Safe Locations: 1 location, 8 families, 25 persons -- down from 2 locations / 16 families / 47 persons on 19 August, as displaced people continue returning home. Nuwara Eliya district remains worst-hit (2,021 families / 7,736 people affected, 6 deaths), followed by Kandy district (1,183 families / 4,925 people affected, 2 deaths).

DMC Situation Report -- Sri Lanka, 26 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL -- 4,248 Families / 16,672 People Affected; Deaths 10; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 747 Partially (749 total); Safe Locations: 1 location, 8 families, 25 persons -- unchanged from the 23 August report. The toll rose from 9 to 10 deaths nationally, with Nuwara Eliya district still worst-hit (2,021 families / 7,736 people affected, 6 deaths), followed by Kandy district (1,186 families / 4,935 people affected, 2 deaths); the additional deaths appear in Hambantota (1) and Puttalam (1) districts, both listed under separate High Wind/Heavy Rain incidents in the same national report.

DMC Situation Report -- Sri Lanka, 04th September 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL -- 4,288 Families / 16,812 People Affected; Deaths 10; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 4 Fully, 781 Partially (785 total), up from 749 on 26 August; Safe Locations: 1 location, 8 families, 25 persons -- unchanged from 26 August. Nuwara Eliya district remains worst-hit; other damages recorded include 1 small/medium enterprise and 2 critical-infrastructure damages nationwide.

DMC Situation Report -- Sri Lanka, 08th September 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL -- 4,290 Families / 16,822 People Affected; Deaths 10; Injured 9; Missing 0; Houses Damaged: 4 Fully, 783 Partially (787 total), up from 785 on 4 September; Safe Locations: 1 location, 8 families, 25 persons -- unchanged since 23 August.

Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre situation report of 9 September 2026 (1000hrs) records 10 deaths, 9 injured and 0 missing, with 4,309 families (16,881 people) affected across the country and 796 houses damaged (4 fully, 792 partially), up marginally from 787 the previous day.

Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre situation report of 13 September 2026 (1000hrs) records 10 deaths, 9 injured and 0 missing, with 4,360 families (17,054 people) affected across the country and 851 houses damaged (4 fully, 847 partially), up from 796 on 9 September, while 25 persons (8 families) remain in 1 safe location, unchanged.

DMC's national daily Situation Report - Sri Lanka (dated 15th September 2026 at 1000hrs) lists only new/ongoing hazard entries for Matale, Matara, Galle, Hambantota, Trincomalee, Ampara, Anuradhapura, Kalutara, Jaffna, Vavuniya, Kegalle and Kurunegala (grand total 935 families/3,842 people affected, 1 death, 2 injured); Nuwara Eliya and Kandy districts -- the districts at the centre of this event -- no longer appear in the report, indicating DMC has stopped actively tracking new impact there.

Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre, Situation Report dated 13 August 2026 at 1000hrs: Grand Total across 14 districts / 8 provinces -- 4,203 families (16,520 people) affected, 9 deaths, 7 injured, 0 missing, 2 houses fully damaged, 707 houses partially damaged, and 263 persons (73 families) currently in 12 safe locations, down from 495 persons (130 families) in the 11 August 2026 1000hrs report. This is the national government's own, more current ground-assessed figure; it supersedes the GDACS Sendai-feed snapshot (12 deaths, static since 6 August), which has not been updated to a new episode since.

DMC Situation Report — Sri Lanka, 14 August 2026 at 1000hrs: GRAND TOTAL — 4,209 Families / 16,536 People Affected; Deaths 9; Injured People 7; Missing People 0; Houses Damaged: 2 Fully, 713 Partially; Safe Location: 9 No. of Safety Locations, 52 Families, 188 Persons.

Disaster Management Centre Sri Lanka, daily situation report (14 August 2026, 1000hrs): 4,209 affected families (16,536 people) nationally, 9 deaths, 7 injured, 0 missing; 715 houses damaged (2 fully, 713 partially); 52 families (188 people) remain in safe/evacuation locations. Nuwara Eliya district is worst-hit (2,021 families / 7,736 people affected, 6 deaths), followed by Kandy district (1,183 families / 4,925 people affected, 2 deaths). No landslide early warning has been issued since 9 August.

description: Floods and landslides across Sri Lanka, centred on Nuwara Eliya and Kandy districts, killed at least 10 people and affected 4,360 families (17,054 people) from mid-August 2026. Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre's figures (10 deaths, 9 injured, 851 houses damaged) held unchanged from 13 to 15 September, and by 15 September the two worst-hit districts no longer appeared in DMC's national daily situation report, indicating the event has stabilised and active impact has ended there.

impact.summary: Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre last recorded 10 deaths, 9 injured and 0 missing for this event, with 4,360 families (17,054 people) affected across the country and 851 houses damaged (4 fully, 847 partially), figures unchanged since 13 September; Nuwara Eliya and Kandy districts, the epicentre of the event, no longer appear in DMC's national daily situation report as of 15 September, indicating the flood and landslide impact there has stabilised.

location.region: Central highlands: Kandy, Nuwara Eliya (including Hatton), Kegalle and Ratnapura districts

event.scale: GDACS Green alert; 10 confirmed deaths (DMC, 13 Sep), 25 people in 1 safe location

name: Floods and Landslides — Sri Lanka

updates.text: Nuwara Eliya and Kandy districts no longer appear in DMC's national daily situation report (15 September), consistent with the event having stabilised after three weeks of unchanged figures; the confirmed toll remains 10 deaths, 9 injured, 4,360 families (17,054 people) affected and 851 houses damaged, last updated by DMC on 13 September.

The DMC's 13 September situation report held deaths at 10 and injured at 9, with affected families rising to 4,360 (17,054 people) and houses damaged to 851 (4 fully, 847 partially), up from 796 on 9 September; the sheltered population held steady at 25 persons (8 families) in 1 safe location.
Sri Lanka DMC's 9 September situation report keeps the death toll at 10 while affected persons edged up to 16,881 (4,309 families) from 16,822, with 796 houses damaged, up from 787.

DMC's 8 September situation report held deaths steady at 10 while affected families/people and houses damaged ticked up marginally to 4,290 families (16,822 people) and 787 houses; the sheltered population remained flat at 25 persons.

The DMC's 4 September situation report held deaths at 10 and injured at 9, with affected families rising to 4,288 (16,812 people) and houses damaged to 785 (4 fully, 781 partially damaged), up from 749 on 26 August; the sheltered population held steady at 25 persons (8 families) in 1 safe location.

The DMC's 26 August situation report recorded the toll rising to 10 deaths (from 9) with 9 injured, as affected families rose to 4,248 (16,672 people) and houses damaged to 749 (2 fully, 747 partially); the sheltered population held steady at 25 persons (8 families) in 1 safe location.

The DMC's 23 August situation report held deaths at 9 and injured at 9, with affected families rising slightly to 4,232 (16,614 people) and houses damaged to 735 (2 fully, 733 partially); the sheltered population fell further to 25 persons (8 families) in 1 safe location, from 47 persons in 2 locations on 19 August.

The DMC's 19 August situation report held deaths at 9 and injured at 9, with the sheltered population unchanged at 47 persons (16 families) in 2 safe locations; affected families edged up to 4,222 (16,583 people) and damaged houses to 725 (2 fully, 723 partially).

The DMC's 17 August situation report recorded 9 deaths and 9 injured (up from 7), with 4,214 families (16,555 people) affected and 720 houses damaged; the sheltered population fell to 47 persons (16 families) in 2 safe locations, from 188 persons (52 families) in 9 locations on 14 August, as displaced people returned home.
No landslide early warning had been issued since 9 August, indicating the acute hazard eased even as daily situation reports and sheltering continued.

The DMC's 14 August report held deaths at 9 with 7 injured; 188 persons (52 families) remained in 9 safe locations, down from 263 persons (73 families) on 13 August, while affected-family and house-damage counts ticked up slightly (4,209 families affected; 713 houses partially damaged).

Sri Lanka's Disaster Management Centre began issuing national situation reports for this event: the 13 August report recorded 9 confirmed deaths and 0 missing, revising the toll down from the GDACS Sendai-feed count of 12 (static since 6 August), with 263 persons (73 families) sheltered, down from 495 on 11 August.
